semanticDefinition: Negative adoption/usage impact risk of acting on this candidate in the tracked environment. It estimates plausible adverse consequences of action, not whether the candidate is important or credible.
exclusions: implementation effort unless it creates a negative use consequence

low.definition: Available evidence supports that acting in the tracked environment has no material negative impact, or only trivial and readily reversible impact. Low requires positive evidence of safe scope/permissions and reversibility; absence of known harm is not enough.
positiveEvidence: scoped permissions and data flows are documented
operation is opt-in, bounded and reversible
relevant deployment/integration path has been inspected
no material adverse side effect is indicated by the evidence
examplesNonNormative: A local opt-in utility using non-sensitive data with narrow permissions and a tested uninstall path.
requiredEvidence: candidate version and intended action/use path
tracked-environment context relevant to the action
evidence refs for permissions, data handling and reversibility

normal.definition: Evidence supports ordinary, bounded or manageable negative consequences if acted upon, with identifiable mitigations; evidence does not meet the LOW or HIGH anchors. Normal is not the missing/unknown value.
positiveEvidence: no credible severe or irreversible downside is identified
negativeEvidence: credible severe harm or unbounded exposure => HIGH
examplesNonNormative: A tool requiring routine permissions and a reversible local configuration change, with documented rollback.
requiredEvidence: candidate version and intended action/use path
evidence of plausible downside and mitigation or rollback

high.definition: Credible evidence shows a material adverse consequence of acting in the tracked environment, including severe data/security/privacy exposure, destructive or difficult-to-reverse change, or significant operational/legal harm.
positiveEvidence: verified broad access to sensitive data without adequate controls
credible serious security/privacy/operational harm in the actual use path
negativeEvidence: only popularity, severity of reported event, weak source credibility, uncertainty, or urgency without an adverse use consequence
examplesNonNormative: A candidate integration transmits tracked-environment secrets to an untrusted endpoint or performs destructive changes with broad privileges.
requiredEvidence: candidate version and intended action/use path
specific adverse consequence and affected asset/data
credible evidence of exposure/exploitability or irreversibility in tracked environment

ambiguityHandling: Missing, conflicting, stale or weakly sourced facts => RISK_UNRESOLVED, no Score Policy invocation. Do not default to normal. Resolve deterministic-source conflicts by source authority/version; if unresolved, do not let model override. Model rubric may classify only after deterministic facts are insufficient and must cite evidence.

provenanceMethods.RULE_FACT: Deterministic explicit source/runtime fact satisfying a named policy rule; takes precedence over model judgment when valid and relevant.
provenanceMethods.MODEL_RUBRIC: Fixed rubric applied to cited evidence only when deterministic facts do not decide the level.
provenanceMethods.HYBRID: Per-candidate resolution chooses RULE_FACT when explicit authoritative facts are decisive; otherwise MODEL_RUBRIC. The resulting value records the actual method, never just HYBRID.

confidenceScale.separateFromScoreInput: Score Policy confidence remains integer 0..10; this provenance confidence is a generation-quality measure and is not passed into scoring.

missingDataBehavior: RISK_UNRESOLVED; candidate remains receipt-only/no score. Never synthesize normal, low, or high from missing evidence.

scorePolicyIntegration.reason: Frozen Score Policy 2.0.1 does not include risk in weighted dimensions, direct bonus, signal, Security Gate or modifier. This candidate preserves that formula; risk affects only the proposed Action Decision Policy.
scorePolicyIntegration.baselineCompatibility: All historical replay rows carry risk=normal; the candidate passes frozen score and signal outputs through unchanged. A future numeric risk penalty/bonus would require a separate policy change and replay review.
